title: createRecord ignores its idempotency replay result: on duplicate it looks up a freshly-minted record_id instead of the original event's, returning InvalidRecord/TransactionFailed
discovered_during: WF03-gh439-testwiring-20260806 step q156 (ISS-0156 / GH #475) — unmasked once the instance_projections fix let createRecord reach its duplicate branch for the first time
symptom:
Replaying createRecord with an already-used idempotency_key does not return the original record. `tests/integration/entity_subsystem_test.zig` block "EXP-202: Create record idempotency" fails at the second createRecord call.

The block asserts the documented EXP-202 contract: r1.is_duplicate == false, r2.is_duplicate == true, r1.record_id == r2.record_id, and exactly one entity_record_latest row for the entity type.
reproduction:
Requires BPM_TEST_DB_URL pointing at a real PostgreSQL, and the ISS-0156 fix applied (otherwise the block fails earlier with InstanceNotFound and never reaches the duplicate branch).

  zig build test-integration-exp

-> block "EXP-202: Create record idempotency" fails at the second createRecord call, with:

  src/entities/commands.zig:433 in fetchRecordResult -> return error.InvalidRecord
  src/entities/commands.zig:144 in createRecord (the duplicate branch)
  tests/integration/entity_subsystem_test.zig:511 (the r2 call)

The same run reports 3 leaked allocations traced to src/event_store/store.zig:1148 (rowToEventRecord) via store.zig:447 — see the secondary defect below.
secondary_defect_same_root:
The duplicate branch also LEAKS the AppendResult it discards. When store.append() detects a duplicate it builds the original EventRecord via rowToEventRecord (src/event_store/store.zig:447), which allocates payload/metadata/event_type strings with the caller's allocator. createRecord's duplicate branch returns immediately at line 144 without freeing `append_res.record`, so those 3 allocations leak on every idempotent replay. The non-duplicate path leaks them too — nothing in createRecord/updateRecord/deleteRecord ever frees append_res.record.

This is the source of the '3 leaks' the test run reports and must be fixed together with the record_id lookup: both live in the same branch and neither is meaningful alone.
impact: The EXP-202 idempotency guarantee does not hold for entity record creation. A client that retries a create after a network timeout — the exact situation idempotency keys exist for — receives an error instead of the original record, and cannot discover the record_id that was actually created. The event store itself is consistent (no duplicate event is written); it is only the command layer's return value that is wrong.
candidate_resolution:
In createRecord's duplicate branch, parse the `record_id` out of `append_res.record.payload` and use THAT for the fetchRecordResult lookup, rather than the locally-minted `record_id`. Set `is_duplicate = true` on the returned RecordResult (fetchRecordResult already does this).

Do not resolve by weakening the test: r1.record_id == r2.record_id is the EXP-202 contract.
notes: Filed separately from ISS-0156 rather than fixed inline: ISS-0156's scope is the missing instance_projections row, and this is an independent logic error in the duplicate branch that merely happened to be unreachable while every append failed with InstanceNotFound. It has its own root cause, its own fix, and its own severity.
